In [ ]:
# INTRODUCTION TO WEB SCRAPING
In [ ]:
# WEB SCRAPING is an automated extraction of large data volumes of data from websites, often converting unstructured HTML 
# into structured formats like CSV,JSON os databases. it is a powerful tool for data collection
In [ ]:
# Before scraping a website, the first thing to do is to inspect the website and for inspecting to be effective,
# one has to understand HTML
In [ ]:
# HTML- Hyper Text Markup Language
# it is the standard markup language for web pages. With html, one can create a website. 
# HTML is also said to be the skeletal part of a web page.It describes the structure of a web page.
In [ ]:
# READ ABOUT - HTML home, basics, element,editor,attribute,heading, paragraph, formating,links,images, table, list,div,class
In [ ]:
# HTML- ELEMENT- HTML consist of series of elements. it tells the browser how to display the content e.g head, paragraph,body
In [ ]:
# HTML EDITOR-it has to do with learning html using notepad (pc) or text edit (mac)
In [ ]:
# HTML FORMATTING - Were designed to display special types of text . for instance, <b>- bold text, <i>- italic text
In [ ]:
# HTML TABLE- It allows webdevelopers to arrange data into rows and columns E.g tr-table row, td- table data, th- table head
In [ ]:
# HTML LIST- allow web developers to group a set of related items in lists
In [ ]:
# HTML DIV- it is used as a container for other html element
In [ ]:
# HTML CLASS- attribute is used to specify a class for an html element. multiple html elements can share the same class

 <script type="text/javascript">
  $(document).ready( function(){
            $("#per_page").change(function(){
                prot = document.location.protocol
                host = 'www.scrapethissite.com'
                path = document.location.pathname
                args = {
                    "per_page": $("#per_page").val(),
                }
                search_val = $("#q").val()
                if (search_val){
                    args["q"] = search_val;
                }
                document.location = prot + '//' + host + path + '?' + $.param(args);
            })
        });
 </script>

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

In [3]:

In [4]:

}
response= requests.get(url, headers=headers)

<div aria-labelledby="firstHeading" class="vector-body" data-mw-ve-target-container="" id="bodyContent">
<div class="vector-body-before-content">
<div class="mw-indicators">
</div>
<div class="noprint" id="siteSub">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</div>
</div>
<div id="contentSub"><div id="mw-content-subtitle"></div></div>
<div class="mw-body-content" id="mw-content-text"><div class="mw-subjectpageheader">
</div><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" dir="ltr" lang="en"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none">List of US companies by revenue</div>
<p class="mw-empty-elt">
</p><p>The first list includes the largest companies in the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a> by <a href="/wiki/Revenue" title="Revenue">revenue</a> as of 2024, according to the <a href="/wiki/Fortune_500" title="Fortune 500"><i>Fortune</i> 500</a> and <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i> rankings. The <i>Fortune</i> 500 list of companies includes only <a href="/wiki/List_of_public_corporations_by_market_capitalization" title="List of public corporations by market capitalization">publicly traded companies</a>, also including <a href="/wiki/Tax_inversion" title="Tax inversion">tax inversion</a> companies. There are also corporations having foundation in the United States, such as corporate headquarters, operational headquarters and independent subsidiaries. However, this list does include several <a href="/wiki/Government-sponsored_enterprise" title="Government-sponsored enterprise">government-sponsored enterprises</a> that were created by acts of <a href="/wiki/United_States_Congress" title="United States Congress">Congress</a> and later became publicly traded.
</p><p>The second list used 2024 data and includes large <a href="/wiki/Privately_held_company" title="Privately held company">privately held companies</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Cargill" title="Cargill">Cargill</a> and <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Koch_Industries" title="Koch Industries">Koch Industries</a>.
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc"/>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="List_of_the_largest_public_/_publicly_traded_companies"><span id="List_of_the_largest_public_.2F_publicly_traded_companies"></span>List of the largest public / publicly traded companies</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=List_of_largest_companies_in_the_United_States_by_revenue&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: List of the largest public / publicly traded companies"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Below are the 100 largest companies by revenue in 2025 (mostly for <a href="/wiki/Fiscal_year" title="Fiscal year">fiscal year</a> 2024), according to the <a href="/wiki/Fortune_500" title="Fortune 500"><i>Fortune</i> 500</a> list.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-:0_1-0"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The following industries are represented in the top 100 largest companies: <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Aerospace_and_defense_industry" title="Aerospace and defense industry">Aerospace and defense</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Agriculture_manufacturing" title="Agriculture manufacturing">agriculture manufacturing</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Airline_industry" title="Airline industry">airline</a>, <a href="/wiki/Automotive_industry" title="Automotive industry">automotive</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Beverage_industry" title="Beverage industry">beverage</a>, <a href="/wiki/Conglomerate_(company)" title="Conglomerate (company)">conglomerate</a>, <a href="/wiki/Energy_industry" title="Energy industry">energy</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Financial_industry" title="Financial industry">financials</a>, <a href="/wiki/Food_industry" title="Food industry">food industry and food processing</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Health_insurance_industry" title="Health insurance industry">health insurance</a>, <a href="/wiki/Healthcare_industry" title="Healthcare industry">healthcare</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Information_technology_industry" title="Information technology industry">information technology</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Insurance_industry" title="Insurance industry">insurance</a>, <a href="/wiki/Machine_industry" title="Machine industry">machinery</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Media_industry" title="Media industry">media</a>, <a href="/wiki/Petroleum_industry" title="Petroleum industry">petroleum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry" title="Pharmaceutical industry">pharmaceutical and pharmacy wholesale</a>, <a href="/wiki/Retail_industry" title="Retail industry">retail</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Technology_industry" title="Technology industry">technology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Telecommunications_industry" title="Telecommunications industry">telecommunications</a>, <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Telecom_hardware_manufacturing" title="Telecom hardware manufacturing">telecom hardware manufacturing</a>, and <a class="mw-redirect" href="/wiki/Transportation_industry" title="Transportation industry">transportation</a>.<sup class="reference" id="cite_ref-:0_1-1"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
